zh.d:
装新版不再多出一份旧程序，早期版本留下的数据会被接管而不是被绕开。

【安装与数据】
· 装过上一版的机器上，安装新版会把旧的那份删掉，而不是在旁边再装一份。上一版的程序目录叫「One Work」（带空格），本版叫「onework」，Windows 把它们当成两个不相干的程序：旧的既不在「添加或删除程序」里、也不会被新版覆盖，于是两份同时躺在磁盘上，用户看到两个一模一样的图标、点开的却是不同版本。真机验证：清掉旧目录后释放 2.24 GB，新版本身完好
· 早期版本留下的数据文件会被改名接管。数据库统一叫 one-backend.db，会话与进程记录同理。此前的做法是「新名字不存在就继续用旧名字」，能用，但每装一次新版就多一条要永远维护的兼容分支，且新旧两套名字可以同时存在。现在启动时直接改名，连 SQLite 的 -wal / -shm 一起搬；万一改到一半失败会回滚，两份都在时不猜、保持原样并记日志

【真实缺陷修复】
· 本地部署的 Ollama 模型现在能保存了。保存时会要求填 API Key，而本机的 Ollama 根本没有 Key，于是这类模型一律保存失败
· Bedrock 拉取模型列表不再要求填 Base URL——它按区域寻址，本就没有这个字段
· Vertex AI 的渠道现在能保存、也能拉到模型列表。真实数据里这个平台名叫 gemini-vertex-ai，而判断逻辑只认 vertex-ai，两处对不上；同时它也不需要 Endpoint
· Gemini 渠道的「刷新模型」按钮点了没反应的问题已修
· 后端进程意外退出时会告诉用户，而不是只写进日志文件——此前界面只是一直转圈
· 对话过程中的上下文与 token 用量现在是实时走的。此前只在整轮结束时更新一次，长任务跑到一半看不出还剩多少余量
· 生成 PPT 时形状尺寸不再离谱地错位。几何数值不带单位时按 EMU 解析（1 厘米 = 360000），写 height=3 得到的是三个 EMU 而不是三厘米，整页排版随之崩掉；officecli 自己的帮助示例就是这么写的
· officecli 的自检循环存在没有出口的分支，会一直转下去
· 「最新优先」的列表在同一毫秒内创建的多条记录上顺序是随机的，现已固定

【界面】
· 「+」菜单里的技能改成可搜索的图标网格，选中的技能以标签形式回显；技能中心与之统一，展示技能自己的名称和图标
· 用户自行导入的技能会进入常驻集合，和内置技能同等对待
· 安装体积继续收窄：不再打包运行时从不会去启动的两个原生 CLI

上一版说明里那句「公司安全策略在本版仍然不会生效」，从本版起不再成立。

【安全策略真正生效】
· 破坏性命令拦截、外网默认拒绝、终端命令审批、发送限流、模型白名单，以及企业记忆的本机召回，执行点都在本机后端。本版把后端提到 v0.1.71-one.4，这部分已经包含在内——管理员在后台配置的策略会下发到成员本机并被真正执行，不再被静默忽略
· 终端命令审批会经公司服务器通道送到成员的桌面客户端
· 渠道的模型白名单在服务端强制；不再拿客户端传来的 id 当服务端的键使用
· 模型代理的用量会记到发起它的那次会话上

【封禁运行节点】
· 被管理员封禁的节点现在真的停止同步团队资源，并且客户端不发机器标识也一样被拒。此前只要客户端不带 x-dream-machine-id 这个头，就会被当成无法判定而放行——封禁只在客户端愿意表明身份时才有效，等于没有
· 浏览器后台不受机器判定影响：管理员自己那台电脑被封禁时，仍然打得开解封它的那个页面
· 本轮在真实二进制上跑通了完整闭环：封禁前放行、封禁后带标识被拒、不带标识同样被拒、同一用户的后台会话仍可用

【退出与清理】
· 退出企业时，加入时下发的九类内容会被逐一收回，此前只收回了其中一部分
· 关闭企业模式后的资源清理改为按证据判断（后端里是否真有企业渠道），不再依赖本地记的一个标记——标记丢了就再也不清理了

en.d:
Installing this version removes the older copy instead of sitting beside it, and adopts the data older builds left behind.

[Install and data]
· On a machine that has the previous version, the installer now deletes it rather than installing a second copy alongside. The previous program directory was "One Work" (with a space), this one is "onework", and Windows treats those as two unrelated programs: the old one appears neither in Add/Remove Programs nor in the new install's path, so both sat on disk at once and the user saw two identical icons opening different versions. Verified on a real machine: 2.24 GB reclaimed, the new install untouched
· Data files from earlier builds are renamed and adopted. The database is now one-backend.db, and the conversation and process records follow the same rule. The previous approach — use the old name when the new one is absent — worked, but added a compatibility branch to maintain forever and allowed both sets of names to exist at once. The rename now happens at startup and carries SQLite's -wal and -shm along with it; a rename that fails part-way rolls back, and two catalogues present is left alone and logged rather than guessed between

[Real defects fixed]
· A locally deployed Ollama model can be saved. Saving demanded an API key, and a local Ollama daemon has none, so every model of this kind failed to save
· Listing Bedrock models no longer asks for a base URL — Bedrock is addressed by region and has no such field
· A Vertex AI channel can now be saved and can list its models. Real rows carry the platform name gemini-vertex-ai while the check only recognised vertex-ai, so the two never met; it also needs no endpoint
· The "refresh models" button on a Gemini channel no longer does nothing when clicked
· When the backend process dies unexpectedly the app says so, instead of recording it only in a log file while the interface keeps spinning
· The context and token meter now moves during a turn. It was updated once, when the whole turn ended, so a long task gave no sense of how much headroom was left while it ran
· Shape geometry in generated PowerPoint decks is no longer wildly misplaced. A geometry number with no unit is read as EMU (1 cm = 360,000), so height=3 means three EMU rather than three centimetres and the layout collapses — which is exactly what officecli's own help example shows
· The officecli self-check loop had a branch with no exit and could spin indefinitely
· A "newest first" listing ordered rows created within the same millisecond arbitrarily; the order is now stable

[Interface]
· Skills in the + menu are a searchable icon grid, with the chosen ones echoed back as chips; the Skills Hub matches, showing each skill's own name and icon
· Skills you import yourself join the always-on set, on the same footing as the built-in ones
· The installed footprint narrows further: two native CLIs the runtime never spawns are no longer bundled

The line in the previous release notes saying company security policy is not enforced no longer applies.

[Security policy is actually enforced]
· Destructive-command blocking, network default-deny, terminal-command approval, send rate limiting, the model allowlist, and local recall of company memory are all enforced by the on-machine backend. This release moves that backend to v0.1.71-one.4, which carries them: the policy an administrator configures is pushed to the member's machine and actually applied, instead of being silently ignored
· Terminal-command approval reaches the member's desktop client over the company-server channel
· A channel's model allowlist is enforced server-side, and client-supplied ids are no longer reused as server keys
· Model-proxy usage is attributed to the conversation that ran it

[Blocking a runtime node]
· A node an administrator blocks now genuinely stops syncing team resources, and a client that sends no machine identifier is refused too. Previously, omitting the x-dream-machine-id header meant the caller could not be judged and was waved through, so the block held only while the client chose to identify itself, which is no block at all
· Browser sessions are exempt from machine scoping, so an administrator whose own laptop is blocked can still open the page that unblocks it
· Verified end to end against the real binary this cycle: allowed before the block, refused with the header, refused without it, while that same user's console session still works

[Leaving and cleanup]
· Leaving a company now takes back all nine kinds of material that joining pushed down; only some of them were being reclaimed
· Cleanup after enterprise mode is turned off is decided on evidence — whether the backend actually holds company channels — rather than on a locally remembered flag that, once lost, meant the cleanup never ran again
